scenes.title: Do these 3 points lie on one straight line?
body: Collinear means points share one straight line.
scenes.narration: Suppose you are given three points: one comma three, three comma seven, and five comma eleven. How can you tell if all three lie on one straight line? Collinear means exactly that. For nonvertical points, compare their slopes.

scenes.title: First compare A to B
body: Slope is change in y divided by change in x.
scenes.narration: Start with A and B. Seven minus three is four, and three minus one is two. Four divided by two equals two, so the slope from A to B is two.

scenes.title: Now compare B to C
body: Use the same slope rule again.
Matching slopes mean the direction did not change.
scenes.narration: Now calculate the slope from B to C. Eleven minus seven is four, and five minus three is two. Again, four divided by two equals two.

scenes.title: Equal slopes mean one line
body: So A, B, and C are collinear.
scenes.narration: Because both slopes equal two, the direction stays constant through all three points. So A, B, and C are collinear. All three also satisfy y equals two x plus one.

scenes.title: Use the shortest reliable test
body: Vertical: check whether every x-coordinate is equal.
scenes.narration: Recap: collinear points share one straight line. For nonvertical points, compare two pairwise slopes. If they match, the points are collinear. For a vertical line, check that all x coordinates are equal. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
